speeds.note: Speeds disagree between Bambu and Prusa; see disagreements. First layer follows Prusa's typical 20 mm/s.

first_layer.bed_first_layer_note: Bambu TDS: 30 to 35 C on Cool or High Temp plates with glue. Prusa lists 60 to 75 C for flexibles and says larger models may need a brim and a slightly higher bed.
first_layer.squish_note: Print the first layer slowly and do not over squish, since TPU squeezes sideways and can feed badly. Use glue stick as a separator on smooth and satin PEI. Textured PEI needs no separator.

walls.note: Softness depends on walls and infill together. Prusa says raise walls and infill for strength and lower the wall and top and bottom layer count to keep the part flexible.

infill.density_note: 10 to 20 percent for a soft part, 30 percent or more for a firmer one. Gyroid gives even give in all directions (expert).

structure.note: Pattern hint is an expert choice; Prusa only gives the wall and infill trade off.

supports.note: Prusa lists support removal as difficult and asks for a Z gap of 0.3 mm and XY separation of at least 100 percent, because close supports stick too hard to TPU. Avoid supports where possible. Bambu warns against many objects with supports on one plate because travel causes stringing. Whether Bambu Support for PLA/PETG works on TPU is not stated by a maker, so test it.

multi_material.note: Standard TPU 95A and TPU 95A HF cannot go through AMS, AMS lite or AMS 2 Pro. The AMS HT works only as a sealed drybox: feed through its dedicated TPU outlet by hand, no auto loading. TPU for AMS is the exception and feeds through every AMS model. Bambu does not support TPU below 85A.

softening_temp_c.note: Orca temperature_vitrification is 30 C. Bambu groups TPU with filaments that soften below 60 C. Bambu star ratings show low heat deflection.

safety.note: Operate in a ventilated area or with filtration, per Bambu. Keep loose filament away from small children and pets.

food_contact.note: Bambu states TPU is not food contact grade. Do not use printed parts for food.

failure_modes.symptom: Filament buckles or wraps around the extruder gears, clicking, no flow
causes: feed path too loose or long

fixes.advice: Feed from a raised, low friction container. Loosen the idler so the gears push gently (Prusa: about 1.5 turns on MK4). Use a filament guide, or unplug the sensor tube on Prusa XL and Core One.

fixes.why: Plain TPU 95A jams above about 3 to 3.6 mm3/s. Slower is more reliable.

fixes.advice: Use a direct drive extruder. Bowden setups cause severe jams with TPU.

failure_modes.symptom: Strings and blobs between parts

fixes.why: TPU is very fluid at temperature. Bambu suggests going down 5 C.
Bambu suggests lowering flow by 0.4 mm3/s together with the temperature drop.
If oozing is severe, Bambu suggests adding 0.2 mm. Keep it small since retraction can jam TPU.
Less travel between models means fewer strings.

fixes.advice: Dry the spool. Wet TPU strings badly.

failure_modes.symptom: Gaps, thin walls, missing layers

fixes.why: Slower flow melts the TPU more fully.

fixes.advice: Cold pull the nozzle, especially after carbon fiber or nylon.
Check for feeding resistance and dry the spool.

failure_modes.symptom: Sagging bridges and droopy overhangs

fixes.why: Slow bridges let the line set.

fixes.advice: Avoid steep overhangs. Use PLA as support and increase the Z gap to about 0.3 mm.

failure_modes.symptom: Part will not release, or pulls PEI coating

fixes.advice: Use glue stick or Kapton as a separator on smooth and satin PEI, or use a textured sheet.

disagreements.resolution: 35 C default on Bambu plates, 50 to 60 C on Prusa sheets. Higher beds help adhesion on large parts.

positions.claim: 30 to 50 percent, cooling off or low

disagreements.resolution: Default to Bambu's values on Bambu printers, Prusa's on Prusa printers. At the very low speeds TPU prints at, either works.

positions.claim: 2.5 mm in the Prusa generic TPU profile, or disable

disagreements.resolution: Default 0.4 mm and go lower if it clogs. The 2.5 mm Prusa value is a shipped default for Nextruder printers.

positions.claim: usually not needed, 60 C for 4 h if damp

disagreements.resolution: Dry it. TPU absorbs moisture fast and Bambu's rule is stricter. Prusament may be dry from the factory, but an opened spool is not.

positions.claim: under 80 mm/s for TPU 95A, under 200 mm/s for TPU 95A HF
20 mm/s typical, 30 to 40 mm/s maximum for flexible filaments

disagreements.resolution: Use the volumetric limit as the real cap: about 3.2 mm3/s on standard TPU, which is 25 to 40 mm/s at 0.2 mm layers. Only the HF and AMS grades go faster.

data.label: Fine detail
data.summary: Miniatures, figurines, embossed text and small features. The nozzle sets the floor: a 0.2 mm nozzle resolves features a 0.4 mm nozzle cannot. Then thin layers, slow walls, enough cooling time per layer, and gentle supports.

changes.why: sleipnir keeps the thinnest layers on domes, slopes and faces and prints straight walls thicker, which saves time without losing detail.
0.08 mm layers make layer lines almost invisible on small models. Bambu's 0.08 mm High Quality preset.
Slow outer walls keep sharp edges on tiny features.
Lower acceleration avoids ringing on small, fast direction changes.
Gentler motion on the visible wall.
Arachne varies line width to fill thin features like swords, fingers and horns that fixed width walls skip.
Keeps walls thinner than two lines instead of dropping them.
Supports only under the steepest overhangs. Fine layers bridge small overhangs on their own. Bambu's 0.08 mm preset uses 15 degrees.
Tree supports touch the model at small points and come off organic shapes more cleanly.
Organic trees grow around the model and are easier to remove from figures.
Tiny layers finish in seconds. Slowing down gives each layer time to cool so heads and spikes do not melt into blobs.
Bambu's finest 0.2 mm nozzle preset. Minimal layer lines.
Matches the 0.2 mm nozzle.
Thin lines need more walls for the same shell thickness. Bambu's 0.2 mm presets use four.

hardware_levers.advice: Swap to a 0.2 mm nozzle for 28 to 32 mm miniatures when one is available. Do not use it with CF, GF or glow filament: the clog risk is very high.

material_hints.note: PLA holds fine detail best. Matte PLA hides layer lines. PETG strings on small travel moves. Filled materials cannot go through a 0.2 mm nozzle.

orientation.advice: Tilt miniatures back 30 to 45 degrees so faces and details are not on the support side.
Print several minis per plate. More travel time per layer lets each one cool, the same effect as a minimum layer time.

data.label: Accurate fit
data.summary: Parts that must mate with other parts: holes for bolts and bearings, press fits, enclosures, gears. Settings get you close. A tolerance test on the actual printer and spool closes the rest.

changes.why: Adjusts outer wall spacing so the shell lands where the model says, and keeps layers more consistent.
Needed for inner, outer, inner wall order.
Orca recommends this order for the best dimensional accuracy: the outer wall is not pushed outward by an inner wall printed after it.
Slower outer walls track corners and small holes more closely.
Turns round holes into polygons sized for the nozzle, so bolts fit without drilling.
Pulls in the first layer so the base is not wider than the part. Bambu's X1 profiles use 0.15 mm.
Fine tunes the last layers so the part's total height matches the model.
Uses the measured hole error from this printer's tolerance test. Positive values make holes bigger.
Uses the measured outside error from the same test.
Scales the part in XY to cancel the shrink this material shows after cooling. Matters most for ABS, ASA, PC and nylon.

prerequisites.why: Over extrusion makes every wall fat and every hole small. Fix flow before compensating.
Measures real hole and contour error for this printer, nozzle and spool.

orientation.advice: Print round holes with their axis vertical. Horizontal holes print as teardrops and come out undersized at the top.

material_hints.note: Filled materials (CF, GF) shrink and warp less. ABS, ASA and unfilled nylon shrink the most; plan on shrink compensation.

data.label: Save filament
data.summary: Use less plastic: cheap props, large decorative pieces, test shapes, or a nearly empty spool. Infill is the cheapest thing to cut. Walls give the most strength per gram, so keep two.

changes.why: Adaptive cubic gets sparse deep inside the part and uses about a quarter less plastic than rectilinear.
Low infill is enough when the part carries no load.
Two walls keep the part stiff. Walls are the best strength per gram.
Lightning only supports the top surfaces and uses the least plastic of any pattern.
Four top layers still close the surface.
Slim trees use less support plastic than grid supports.

checks: Compare grams before and after in the slice summary and report the saving.
If the loaded spool has less filament than the job needs, say so before slicing further (Spoolman or AMS remaining weight).

data.label: Flexible
data.summary: Parts that bend, squeeze or seal: phone cases, gaskets, bumpers, straps, feet. Flexibility comes first from the material (TPU hardness) and second from the geometry: fewer walls and low, even infill make a part softer. Flexible filament prints slowly because it buckles in the extruder.

material_fallback.when: The loaded material is not TPU
material_fallback.advice: Real flex needs TPU. PETG bends a little and springs back on thin sections; PLA snaps. Ask before switching material.

changes.why: Each extra wall makes TPU stiffer. Two walls keep a phone case soft enough to fit over the edges.
Gyroid flexes about the same in every direction, so the part does not have a hard axis.
Low infill lets the part compress. Raise it for firmer parts.
TPU buckles if pushed fast. Orca's generic TPU is capped at 3.2 mm3/s and Bambu TPU 85A at 2.2.
Long retractions stretch and jam soft filament. Orca's TPU profiles use 0.4 mm.
With little retraction, fast travel is what keeps strings short.
A third wall firms up bumpers and feet that need to hold shape.
More infill for parts that carry weight, like printer feet.

hardware_rules.advice: Use a direct drive extruder. Bowden printers struggle with TPU 95A and rarely handle 85A.
Feed TPU from an external spool holder, not the Bambu AMS or AMS lite. Only products sold as TPU for AMS go through the AMS.
Dry TPU before printing; it is marked drying required.

orientation.advice: Print phone cases standing on the back face so the lip prints as clean walls.

data.label: Food contact (caveats)
data.summary: Cookie cutters, cups, bowls, utensils. mimir never calls an FDM print food safe. It explains the risks, applies the watertight settings where they help, and suggests safer options. The caveats are always shown, whatever else the user asks for.

caveats.text: Layer lines and gaps trap food and bacteria that washing cannot remove. Prusa does not recommend printed parts as food containers.
Brass nozzles can contain about 2 percent lead. Use a stainless steel nozzle for anything that touches food.
Most filament colorants are not certified for food contact, even when the base resin is.
A food safe epoxy coating seals the surface. Otherwise treat the part as single use, such as a cookie cutter used once.
Hot drinks and dishwashers soften PLA (about 55 C) and can deform PETG near 70 C.

changes.why: Dense walls leave fewer gaps for food to get into.
Slightly more plastic closes gaps between lines.
Concentric top lines follow the outline of a cutter or rim, leaving fewer crossing grooves.

material_hints.note: Prefer natural (uncolored) PETG or PLA from a maker that publishes food contact documents. Avoid styrenics and fiber filled materials.

hardware_rules.advice: Require a stainless steel or hardened nozzle that is certified lead free. Ask if the printer still has a brass nozzle.

data.label: Heat resistant
data.summary: Parts that live in a hot car, near a motor, in a printer enclosure or in sunlight. Heat resistance is almost entirely a material choice. Settings cannot make PLA survive a dashboard. mimir picks a material whose softening temperature clears the stated use temperature with margin.

selection.rule: Pick filaments with properties.softening_temp_c.typical at least 15 C above the stated use temperature. If none is loaded, propose one and ask.

pa_cf.note: Orca vitrification value. Bambu PAHT-CF lists Vicat 220 C.

use_temperature_hints.note: Closed cars in summer sun routinely pass 70 C on the dash. Treat as 80 C.

changes.why: Thicker walls resist sagging and creep when the part is warm.
Denser infill keeps a warm part from slowly collapsing under load.

pla.advice: Annealing PLA at 100 C for 45 min raises heat resistance but shrinks the part up to 10 percent in XY and grows it in Z, with unpredictable warping. Choose PETG, ASA or PC instead unless the part is simple and you can scale for it.

material_hints.note: Carbon fiber does not rescue PLA: PLA-CF softens near 50 C.

data.summary: Worked parses of typical requests. mimir's model turns text into an intent (goals with levels, material, quantity, deadline, constraints); kb.intent merges the goals; settings.plan turns the result into a diff. These examples anchor the parse and double as few shot examples in the system prompt.

intent_shape.material: filament id from knowledge/filaments, or null to use what is loaded
intent_shape.constraints: printer ids, nozzle, max grams, plates
intent_shape.ask: questions mimir must ask before planning, if any

examples.text: I want 12 functional brackets in PETG, strong, by tomorrow

intent.deadline: tomorrow 09:00 local unless the user says otherwise

notes: Strength and speed conflict: keep 4 walls, 25 percent gyroid and a hot nozzle; take layer height 0.24 mm from speed (tradeoffs strength and speed).
Orient each bracket on its side so the bend is in the layer plane.
Check PETG stock and which printers have PETG loaded, then spread plates across them before cutting quality.
Textured PEI, no glue. Smooth PEI only with glue stick.
Vase mode with a 0.6 mm line on a 0.4 mm nozzle, 3 or more bottom layers.
Silk PLA is limited to about 7.5 mm3/s in Orca's generic profile; keep it. Silk shine hides layer lines, so 0.2 mm layers are fine.
Surface finish changes that need several walls (inner, outer, inner order) do not apply in vase mode; skip them and say so.

ask: Is the TPU fed from an external spool? It should not go through the AMS unless it is a TPU for AMS product.
notes: Two walls, 15 percent gyroid, max volumetric speed about 3.2 mm3/s, retraction 0.4 mm or less.
Dry the spool first. Print on textured PEI at 35 C or so; TPU sticks hard to smooth PEI.
Needs an enclosed printer. If the target printer is open frame (A1, A1 mini, P1P, MK4S without enclosure), say so and propose an enclosed one.
Keep fan low for ASA, use a brim on large flat parts, turn on air filtration where the printer has it.
0.28 mm layers, 2 walls, lightning infill at 10 percent, support only below 40 degrees.
Say plainly that lightning infill has no strength.

ask: Is a 0.2 mm nozzle available? It resolves much finer detail than 0.4 mm.
notes: 0.08 mm layers on 0.4 mm (0.06 mm on 0.2 mm), outer wall 60 mm/s, Arachne, organic tree supports, minimum layer time on.
Recommend tilting the model so the face is not on the support side.
4 walls, nozzle 5 C hotter, flow up 5 percent, 5 bottom layers, infill and wall overlap 25 percent, scarf seams.
If the loaded material is PLA, suggest PETG for anything that stays wet or warm.
If the container is for food, add the food contact caveats.

ask: Is the nozzle hardened steel? PA-CF wears brass and stainless nozzles quickly.
Has the spool been dried in the last day? Nylon is marked drying required.
notes: Refuse to plan on a non hardened nozzle. Prefer a 0.6 mm hardened nozzle; 0.4 mm works for fine teeth.
Enclosed printer, Engineering plate or textured PEI with glue, fan low, keep the spool in a dry box while printing.
Print the gear flat so teeth are in the layer plane. Six walls make the teeth nearly solid.
Run a tolerance test first if it meshes with other gears or sits on a shaft.

data.label: Fast
data.summary: Finish sooner. On modern printers the limit is usually how much plastic the hotend can melt per second (max volumetric speed), not the speed numbers. The real levers are thicker layers, a bigger nozzle, less infill and fewer top layers. Raising mm/s past the melt limit changes nothing.

changes.why: Thicker layers mean fewer layers. 0.24 mm on a 0.4 mm nozzle matches Bambu's Draft preset.
Infill is hidden, so keep it at the stock 15 percent.
Grid is one of the fastest patterns and is the Bambu default.
Four top layers still close the surface at thicker layer heights, as in Bambu's Draft preset.
Prints sparse infill every second layer at double height, which saves time inside the part.
0.28 mm on a 0.4 mm nozzle is Bambu's Extra Draft height. Layer lines show, and that is fine for a test fit.
Two walls are enough for a shape check.
Lightning infill only holds up the top surfaces and uses the least plastic. Use it for looks only, never for load.
Lightning at low density is enough to carry the top skin.
Only the steepest overhangs get support, as in Bambu's Extra Draft preset.

hardware_levers.advice: A 0.6 mm nozzle at 0.30 mm layers moves much more plastic per pass. Bambu ships 0.30 mm Standard and Strength presets for it. Suggest it for large parts when one is available (hardened steel handles every material).
High flow filament and a high flow hotend raise the melt limit. Bambu PETG HF runs 21 mm3/s on a standard X1C hotend and 29 on the high flow one.
Split the job across idle printers with the same material before cutting quality.

limits: Never exceed the filament's max volumetric speed; the slicer caps speeds there anyway, so raising mm/s is pointless.
Do not raise acceleration above the printer profile. Input shaping and the profile already set the safe ceiling.
Keep first layer settings. A failed first layer costs more time than it saves.

data.label: Strong
data.summary: Parts that carry load, get bolted down, snap together or get dropped. Walls and temperature matter more than infill. Orientation matters most of all: layers are the weak direction.

changes.why: Walls carry most of the load. Four walls held 33 kg in CNC Kitchen's hook test where two walls held 20 kg.
25 percent infill backs up the walls without much extra time. Bambu's Strength preset uses the same value.
Gyroid is about equally strong in every direction, so the part does not have a weak axis.
Thicker top skins spread point loads from screws and clips.
A thicker base stops the first layers from cracking under a bolt head.
Layers bond best near the upper end of the filament's range. PLA peaked at 230 C and PETG at 245 C in layer adhesion tests; hotter than that gets weaker again.
Keeps every layer between about 30 and 50 percent of the nozzle, the band where layers bond best; parts weaken once layers pass half the nozzle.
Six walls make most small parts nearly solid where it counts. This matches Bambu's Strength preset.
Wider inner walls bond better. Layer adhesion peaked near 150 percent of nozzle width, and the outside of the part looks the same.
Wider infill lines are stronger and print in fewer passes.
Past this point walls give more strength per gram than more infill.
A slower outer wall lays down a denser, more even skin. Bambu's Strength preset runs it at 60 mm/s.
An extra wall every other layer wedges the infill between walls for a stronger bond. Orca requires turning off ensure vertical shell thickness with it.
Required by alternate extra wall.

change.why: Less part cooling keeps each layer hot long enough to fuse with the next.

cooling_rule.note: Do not cut fan for PLA family. PLA needs cooling for overhangs, and its bond is already strong at the upper temperature.

orientation.advice: Lay the part so the load runs along the layers, never across them. Lying samples reached about 60 MPa in PLA while layer to layer bonds peaked at 40 MPa.
For brackets and hooks, print on the side so the bend is in the XY plane.

material_hints.note: PLA is stiff and strong but brittle and creeps under steady load or warmth. PETG is tougher. For heat or long term load, step up to ASA, PC or nylon composites.

checks: In preview, confirm walls reach the requested count on thin features (Arachne may merge them).
Estimate time again. More walls and hotter temperatures can push the job past a deadline; see tradeoffs.

data.label: Smooth surface
data.summary: Visible parts where the outside matters: display pieces, gifts, product shells. Slow and gentle outer walls, finer layers, a hidden or scarfed seam, and ironing on flat tops. Inner walls and infill stay fast.

changes.why: Thin layers go where stair steps show on curves and shallow slopes; vertical walls stay thicker and faster.
Thinner layers make the steps on curves smaller. Bambu's High Quality presets start at 0.16 mm.
A slow outer wall shows fewer ripples and more even gloss. Bambu's High Quality presets use 60 mm/s.
Gentler acceleration on the visible wall cuts ringing near corners.
Matches Bambu's High Quality presets, which trade time for a calmer surface.
A slower top skin lies flatter.
A scarf seam ramps the start and end of each outer loop so the seam line nearly disappears and gets stronger.
Lines the seam up toward the back of the part where it is least visible.
Inner, outer, inner wall order needs at least three walls.
The outer wall prints undisturbed from an inner wall for the best finish. Overhangs get slightly worse, so skip this on parts with steep overhangs.
Monotonic lines all run the same way, so the top reflects light evenly.
Leaves more room for the top pattern on flat faces, so tops look like one continuous sheet.
0.08 mm layers make lines almost invisible, at a large time cost. Bambu's 0.08 mm High Quality preset.
Ironing runs the hot nozzle over the top surface a second time to smooth it. Works only on flat tops.
Orca's default 10 percent flow fills the tiny gaps without ridges.
Orca default spacing, well under the nozzle width.
Orca default. Slow passes iron best.

rules.text: Only suggest ironing when the model has large flat top faces. It does nothing on curved or organic tops.
Silk PLA hides layer lines by itself. Keep its low volumetric limit instead of speeding up the walls.
Matte PLA already hides lines and seams. Ironing polishes matte tops and makes them look patchy, so leave it off.

orientation.advice: Face the most visible side away from supports and keep it vertical or on top. Support contact always leaves marks.
For a glossy or textured bottom face, pick the plate for the look: smooth PEI for glossy, textured PEI for a grain.

data.summary: How kb.intent merges several goals into one set of changes. Goals rarely conflict on every key; most conflicts are on a few speed and structure keys. The rules below decide who wins and what mimir tells the user.

examples: printer max hotend and bed temperature
abrasive filament needs a hardened nozzle
ventilation for ABS, ASA and PC

precedence.what: Goals the user stated in words
Goals mimir inferred from the model or the material
examples: vase shaped model suggests vase mode

merge_rules.rule: When two goals move a key the same way, keep the stronger bound (the larger at_least, the smaller at_most).

When an at_least from one goal is above an at_most from another, the higher ranked goal wins. If both are stated goals, the goal listed first in the conflicts table below wins, and mimir says what it gave up.
When two goals set a key to different values, use the pair rule below. If none exists, keep the value from the stated goal and flag it.
A change marked priority core in one goal beats a change marked supporting in another.
After merging, clamp every value to settings.yaml bounds and to the filament and printer limits. Report every clamp.

pairs.resolution: Keep the walls and the temperature from strength (they are cheap in time and carry the load). Take layer height and infill pattern from speed. Infill density goes to the strength floor, not the speed ceiling.
pairs.never: Never use lightning infill for a part that carries load.
pairs.tell_user: Kept four walls for strength and used thicker layers to save time.

pairs.resolution: Both can hold. Slow only the outer wall; inner walls and infill stay fast. Wall order inner, outer, inner still gives strong walls.
They pull opposite ways on walls and infill. Ask which matters more. A tough but bendy part usually means TPU 95A with three walls.
pairs.ask: Should it bend and spring back, or hold its shape under load?

pairs.resolution: Vase mode is one line thick. Refuse the combination unless the user accepts a fragile part; offer a wide line (1.5 times the nozzle) or normal mode with two walls and no top.
pairs.ask: Vase mode makes a single wall. Do you want the seamless look or a stronger part?

pairs.resolution: Keep walls, cut infill. Walls give the most strength per gram.
Slow only the outer wall and the top surface. Everything hidden runs at speed. Layer height is the real conflict: offer 0.16 mm as the middle ground.
Detail needs thin layers, which are slow. Keep 0.08 to 0.12 mm and save time by batching several models per plate instead.
pairs.tell_user: Fine layers take time. Printing several at once is the fastest way to more models.

pairs.resolution: Slow only the outer wall. Keep compensation settings; they cost nothing.
Keep walls, flow and temperature from watertight. Vase mode is both fast and seamless if the shape allows it.
Compatible. Use vase mode with a line width of at least 1.5 times the nozzle and five bottom layers.
Heat resistance picks the material first. If the loaded spool cannot meet the use temperature, stop and propose a material before changing settings.
Same as heat resistance: the material decides. ASA needs an enclosure; check the printer before planning.
Never drops the caveats. Food contact never unlocks materials outside its prefer list without an explicit user confirmation.

deadline.summary: "By tomorrow" or "by Friday" is a time budget. mimir slices with the goal settings, estimates wall clock time across the printers that can run the material, and only spends quality when the plan misses the deadline.
budget_rules: Budget is the time until the deadline minus a 20 percent margin for failures and plate changes, and minus hours nobody can clear a plate (ask if unknown).
Count parallel printers: wall clock time is the longest single printer queue, not the sum.

levers_in_order.what: Spread plates across more idle printers loaded with the same material (or with the material in their AMS).
Fill each plate. One long plate beats several short ones because of heat up, leveling and flow calibration time.
Raise layer height toward 0.6 to 0.7 times the nozzle diameter.
Suggest a 0.6 mm nozzle when the printer has one; never swap hardware without approval.
Lower infill density down to the floor of the strongest stated goal.
Drop top and bottom layers to the minimum the layer height allows.
Move speed from standard to draft only for parts with no stated strength or surface goal.

never_cut: wall_loops below a stated strength level
deadline.report: State the estimate, the deadline, which levers were used and what each cost in quality.

data.label: Outdoor and UV
data.summary: Parts that live outside: garden fittings, mounts, signs, car exterior parts. Sunlight, heat and water together. ASA is the default outdoor material. It prints like ABS, so it needs an enclosure and good ventilation.

changes.why: Thick walls keep water out of the infill and survive years of sun cycling.
A closed top skin stops rain from pooling inside the part.
Seals the base against standing water.

notes.text: ASA has high UV and weather resistance.
PLA softens in summer sun (about 55 C) and becomes brittle outdoors over time.
ABS prints like ASA but yellows and weakens in sunlight; prefer ASA for anything outside.
PETG is a reasonable outdoor fallback in mild climates up to about 70 C.

printer_requirements.advice: ASA needs an enclosed printer to avoid warping and cracking between layers.
ASA gives off fumes. Use the printer's filter or vent the room.

data.label: Spiral vase
data.summary: Single wall prints that spiral up without a seam: vases, lamp shades, planters, cups. Fast and beautiful, but the wall is one line thick, so it is fragile and holds water only if the line is wide enough.

changes.why: Prints the outer wall as one continuous spiral with no seam.
Vase mode prints a single wall.
There is no inside to fill.
The top stays open.
Vase mode cannot print supports.
A solid floor of three or more layers. Raise it for planters or anything holding water.
A wider single line (0.6 mm on a 0.4 mm nozzle) makes the wall stronger and watertight.
Smooths the XY moves too, so no seam shows even on sloped walls.

constraints.text: One object per plate. Multiple objects print one at a time or not at all.
The model must be a solid. A model with its own inner wall prints both surfaces.
Layer time gets short near a narrow top. Keep minimum layer time on so the rim does not sag.

material_notes.pla_silk: Silk PLA is the classic vase material. Keep its low max volumetric speed; the wall speed is capped by melt rate anyway.
material_notes.petg: Good for planters and outdoor vases. Wide lines seal well.

data.label: Watertight
data.summary: Containers, planters, cups (non food), funnels and enclosures that must hold water or keep it out. Leaks start at gaps between lines and at the seam. More walls, a little more plastic, hotter layers and good overlap close them.

changes.why: Prusa recommends 3 to 4 walls for a watertight single wall, more for tricky shapes.
5 to 10 C above the preset fuses lines together with no pinholes. Stay inside the filament's range.
About 5 percent more plastic closes the tiny gaps between lines.
0.15 to 0.2 mm layers bond most reliably. Keep layers under about 60 percent of the nozzle width.
Prusa suggests 25 to 35 percent overlap between infill and walls if a part leaks.
Closes lids and tops fully.
The floor of a container takes the pressure; five solid layers seal it.
Adds solid infill under sloped walls so the shell never gets thin.
Scarf seams overlap the start and end of each loop, so the seam is not a weak line where water gets in.

vase_option.when: Single walled, open top shape with no internal features
vase_option.note: Spiral vase has no seam at all. Widen the line to 0.6 mm or more on a 0.4 mm nozzle so the single wall seals.

material_hints.note: PETG bonds layers very well and is a common choice. ASA and ABS can also be sealed with an acetone vapor or wipe.

post_processing.advice: For anything that must never leak, coat the inside with epoxy or a sealant after printing.

data.name: Bambu Lab A1
data.status_note: Listed in the Bambu US store in 2026-09.

extruder.note: Store table does not state the extruder gear material.

hotend.note: Toolless hotend swap in a few minutes. A high flow hotend is sold. Sync the nozzle info on the screen after a swap.

bed.note: Store lists Textured PEI (included), Smooth PEI, Dual-Texture PEI, High Temperature Plate and Cool Plate. SuperTack fits per the Bambu plate guide.

motion.note: Store says 10000 mm/s2. The Orca machine profile carries 12000. Slicer profile default is 6000 for printing.

max_w.note: At 220 V. 350 W at 110 V. Bambu wiki table only, the store spec page does not list electrical figures.

printing_typical_w.note: Bambu wiki average power over a short test print (about 17 to 19 minutes).

idle_w.note: Bambu wiki reading without network connection. 4.1 to 5.4 W with Wi-Fi.

measured_examples.job: Bambu wiki test print, PLA, 16 min 58 s
Bambu wiki test print, ABS, 18 min 35 s

data.sensors_note: Force sensor is what Bambu calls the extrusion force or eddy current sensor in the toolhead. Camera is low frame rate, up to 1080p.

builtin_calibrations.what: Auto K value. The toolhead purges at the wiper and reads extrusion force with its eddy current sensor. Needs firmware 01.04.00.00 or newer.
Automatic bed leveling and nozzle height.
Resonance compensation. Rerun after moving the printer.
Touch probe test outside the bed that catches a nozzle wrapped in molten filament.

multi_material.note: Cannot be combined with other AMS models.

multi_material.needs: A1 series AMS Hub, firmware 01.07.00.00 or newer. Do not use the X1 or P1 buffer or hub.
A1 series AMS Hub and a power adapter for drying

materials.note: Store: PLA, PETG, TPU, PVA ideal; ABS, ASA, PC, PA, PET and fiber reinforced not recommended (open frame). PLA-CF and PETG-CF need a hardened nozzle. TPU feeds from the external spool, not the AMS lite.

pilot_notes: Open frame bedslinger. Block ABS, ASA, PC and nylon or warn strongly. Bambu rates them not recommended here.
The bed moves in Y, so tall thin parts wobble more. Keep the model footprint wide and reduce speed or acceleration on tall parts.
Time-lapse on A series moves the bed and toolhead to a fixed shooting spot every layer. Smooth mode adds a prime tower. Traditional mode hides ooze in infill and needs infill on each layer.
AMS lite feeds only rigid enough filament: no TPU softer than 77D, no absorbent PVA, no third party CF or GF. Use the external spool for those.
The nozzle swap is toolless. After a swap to another diameter or the high flow hotend, sync the nozzle on the screen and rerun flow dynamics.
Auto flow dynamics reads force from the toolhead. A third party hotend and 0.2 mm nozzles can produce bad results.
Build plate position detection can be turned off in print options if the plate is not recognized.

common_issues.symptom: Nozzle wraps in filament (clumping) and the print stops
common_issues.cause: First layer did not stick, so plastic dragged and wrapped the nozzle.

fix.advice: Wash the plate, or add glue stick, and rerun. Clumping detection is an aid, not a guarantee.

fix.why: A slower first layer gives lines time to bond.

common_issues.symptom: AMS lite tangle alarm or failed loads
common_issues.cause: PTFE tube too long or bent, or filament the feeder cannot push.

fix.advice: Place the AMS lite about 50 mm from the printer with short tubes. Put heavy spools in slots 2 and 3.

common_issues.symptom: Flow dynamics calibration fails on 0.2 mm nozzle
common_issues.cause: Bambu says all printers with a 0.2 mm hotend often fail auto calibration.

fix.advice: Use the manual K pattern with the 0.2 mm nozzle.

positions.claim: 12000 mm/s2 in the Orca machine profile

disagreements.resolution: Use 10000 as the hardware figure. The slicer process profile prints at 6000.

data.name: Bambu Lab A1 mini
data.status_note: Listed in the Bambu US store in 2026-09.

hotend.note: The A1 hotend page covers the A1 series and its toolless design. A high flow hotend is documented for A1, not stated for the mini.

bed.note: 80 C is low. Do not plan PETG on a hot bed above 80 C or any high temperature filament.

motion.note: Store says 10000 mm/s2. The Orca machine profile carries 20000. The slicer process profile prints at 6000.

max_w.note: Same figure at 110 V and 220 V. Bambu wiki table only, the store spec page does not list electrical figures.

printing_typical_w.note: Bambu wiki average power over a short test print (about 18 to 23 minutes).

idle_w.note: Bambu wiki reading without network connection. 6.1 to 7.3 W with Wi-Fi.

measured_examples.job: Bambu wiki test print, PLA, 17 min 54 s
Bambu wiki test print, PETG, 23 min 13 s

power.note: The wiki lists no voltage range for the A1 mini. Its 150 W limit is the lowest of any printer in this set.

builtin_calibrations.what: Auto K value using the toolhead force (eddy current) sensor at the purge wiper. Needs A series firmware 01.04.00.00 or newer.
Automatic bed leveling.
Resonance compensation.

multi_material.note: Shipped tubes in the mini combo are 580 and 700 mm. Keep them short to avoid false tangle alarms.

materials.note: Store: PLA, PETG, TPU, PVA ideal; ABS, ASA, PC, PA, PET and fiber reinforced not recommended.

pilot_notes: Build volume is 180 mm on each axis. Check part fit before slicing and suggest splitting or scaling.
Bed maxes at 80 C. Cap bed temperature at 80 for PETG and use Textured PEI or SuperTack.
Open frame. Block ABS, ASA, PC, nylon and fiber grades.
AMS lite limits apply: no soft TPU, no third party CF or GF, no absorbent PVA in the AMS.
The default process profile has no elephant foot compensation (0), unlike the A1 (0.075).

common_issues.symptom: Nozzle clumping alarm mid print
common_issues.cause: First layer lifted and the nozzle wrapped in filament.

fix.advice: Wash the plate or add glue stick. Slow the first layer.

fix.why: A slower first layer gives lines time to bond.

common_issues.symptom: Excess purge or false tangle alarms with AMS lite
common_issues.cause: Tubes too long for the mini.

fix.advice: Cut or reposition the tubes so the AMS lite sits close to the printer.

positions.claim: 20000 mm/s2 in the Orca machine profile

disagreements.resolution: Use 10000 as the hardware figure.

data.name: Bambu Lab A2L

max_flow_mm3s.note: Bambu test: 150 mm round model, single wall, Bambu PLA Basic at 220 C.

power.mains: High voltage version 200 to 240 V AC, low voltage version 100 to 120 V AC, 50/60 Hz

max_w.note: 1000 W at 220 V and 1000 W at 110 V. Voltage is fixed per sales region.

standby_w.note: Offline standby. 5.1 to 5.5 W with Wi-Fi.

printing_typical_w.note: Bambu wiki gives 0.145 kWh measured over 1 hour of PLA printing, which is an average of 145 W.

measured_examples.job: Bambu wiki 1 hour PLA print

power.note: The spec sheet says the heatbed holds maximum power for about 3 minutes to reach temperature quickly.

multi_material.note: Up to 4 AMS units plus 1 AMS lite, up to 19 colors. A 4-in-1 PTFE adapter for two or more.

pilot_notes: Large open frame bedslinger with a 330 x 320 x 325 mm volume and an 80 C bed. Treat like an A1 for filament limits: PLA, PETG, TPU and PVA. PLA-CF and PETG-CF need a hardened nozzle.
Bambu ships a cutting module for the A2L family. Ignore it for slicing.

data.name: Bambu Lab AMS (first generation)
data.compatibility_notes: X1 and P1 need a filament buffer for one unit or an AMS Hub for several, up to 4 units. A series needs the A1 series AMS Hub and firmware 01.07.00.00 or newer; do not use the X1 or P1 buffer there. H2 series has the buffer built in.

drying.humidity_display: Levels A to E, not a percentage.

notes: Standard TPU is marked not compatible with AMS in the Bambu table. Only TPU for AMS and TPU 95A HF are marked compatible.
Bambu PA-CF and PAHT-CF are compatible. Third party fiber filled nylon is not listed as compatible.
PET-CF/GF, PPA-CF/GF and PPS-CF/GF are not compatible.
PLA Glow is not recommended.

rfid.detail: Two RFID boards read the tags on both sides of Bambu spools. Read on insertion, on startup or manually per slot. The reading also estimates remaining filament. Reading is unavailable while the slot is loaded to the extruder.

features: Preloading pulls filament in to the hub when a spool is inserted.
Auto mapping matches slicer filaments to AMS slots by type first, then color.
Auto refill switches to another slot with the same brand, type, color and nozzle temperature when a spool runs out.

known_issues.symptom: Auto refill does not switch to a backup spool
known_issues.cause: Backup spool differs in brand, type, color or nozzle temperature, or the user paused and unloaded during the print.

fix.advice: Load a spool with the identical brand, type and color in another slot, and enable AMS Auto-Refill in AMS settings. Do not pause and unload mid print.

known_issues.symptom: Last piece of filament cannot be pulled back and the next color contaminates
known_issues.cause: The tail has left the spool, so the AMS cannot retract it during a color change.

fix.advice: The printer flushes the tail before switching slots. Wait for the purge and let the screen prompt finish.

known_issues.symptom: RFID is not read after a multi plate run without unloading
known_issues.cause: If filament stays in the toolhead the AMS is not idle.

fix.advice: Restore the unload G-code, or unload the slot and use Re-Read.

known_issues.symptom: Purged filament jams the chute on long multi color prints
known_issues.cause: Waste piles up or a cover blocks the chute.

fix.advice: Use a large catch container, keep the chute open and empty it during the print.

fix.why: Bambu says defaults run high. Verify colors stay clean.

data.name: Bambu Lab AMS 2 Pro
data.compatibility_notes: X1 and P1: buffer or AMS Hub required, up to 4 units. A series: A1 series AMS Hub, firmware 01.07.00.00 or newer. H2 series and X2D: buffer built in, up to 4 AMS 2 Pro plus 8 AMS HT. P2S: P2S buffer needed unless a combo. Use the new 6-pin cable that ships with AMS 2 Pro.

drying.max_temp_note: The maximum is reachable only when ambient is 25 C or warmer.

tpu.note: May not fully dry TPU. Bambu suggests the bed or AMS HT.

drying.power: H2 series, P2S and X2D power one AMS 2 Pro from the printer. Extra units and X1, P1, A1 series and A2L units need the 24 V 4 A Switching Adapter.
drying.modes: Rotating spool drying is recommended and turns each spool 30 degrees every 5 minutes. Static drying is not for PLA, PVA, support for PLA/PETG and TPU.
drying.while_printing: The AMS lowers drying to 45 C if PLA is loaded, or 55 C when PETG is loaded during a print.
drying.remove_before_hot_drying: Pull PLA and TPU out before drying PETG or hotter materials.

notes: Same filament rules as the AMS: TPU only in TPU for AMS and TPU 95A HF grades. Feed soft TPU from the external spool or the AMS HT TPU outlet.
Hot materials (ABS, ASA, PC, PA) load fine but cannot be dried here. Dry them elsewhere or in an AMS HT.

rfid.detail: Two RFID coils read official spool tags and feed remaining filament estimation and auto backup.

features: Humidity and temperature sensor in the front of the cabin, shown on the screen, Studio and Handy.
Color changing silicone desiccant: yellow turns purple when spent.
Two actively controlled air vents, intake at the bottom and exhaust at the rear. Keep them clear.

known_issues.cause: Ambient below 25 C, or the printer is feeding or printing while it powers the unit (power drops to about 86 percent on H2 series).

fix.advice: Use the 24 V Switching Adapter and dry in a warmer room or insulate the unit.

known_issues.symptom: Filament softens or deforms during hot drying
known_issues.cause: PLA or TPU left in the AMS while drying PETG or ABS class materials.

fix.advice: Remove all PLA and TPU from the AMS before drying anything hotter.

known_issues.cause: Older first generation 6-pin cable used with AMS 2 Pro.

fix.advice: Use the new 6-pin cable that ships with AMS 2 Pro and AMS HT.

known_issues.symptom: P2S or X2D cannot heat or move during drying
known_issues.cause: The printer allocates its power to the AMS when no power adapter is connected.

fix.advice: Connect the Switching Adapter so printing can run while drying.

data.name: Bambu Lab AMS HT
data.compatibility_notes: Single spool unit. X1 and P1 need a buffer or AMS Hub, A series needs the A1 series AMS Hub. H2 series and X2D take up to 8 AMS HT units. Every unit needs external power for drying, whatever the printer.

drying.heater: 170 W heater. Holds 85 C in 10 to 25 C ambient.

tpu.note: Appendix table gives 75 C for 18 h; the material table says 12 h.

drying.power: Own power cable, included. It never draws printer power.
drying.lid_sensor: Printer warns if the lid opens during drying.

drying_w.note: Matches the 170 W heater listed under drying.

notes: TPU has a dedicated outlet at the rear of the lid. Auto feed and unload do not work with TPU there. The unit still dries it.
Bambu does not publish a separate AMS HT column in the filament compatibility table. The list above follows the AMS column plus the AMS HT drying table, which covers PA, PC, PVA and fiber grades.

rfid.detail: RFID coil in the unit. Bambu publishes a coil replacement guide.

features: Front display shows humidity, temperature and remaining drying time.
Filament release button behind the inlet to pull filament out by hand.
Outlet hall sensor locates a broken or jammed filament.

known_issues.symptom: Nylon, PC or PVA still wet after a drying run
known_issues.cause: Spool absorbed a lot of moisture, or PVA, PPS-CF or PPA-CF need more heat than 85 C.

fix.advice: Use the material table time (for example PA 85 C for 12 h) and repeat. For PPA-CF and PPS-CF use a convection oven or the bed.

known_issues.symptom: TPU will not feed from the AMS HT

fix.advice: Route TPU out of the rear TPU outlet and push it into the extruder by hand.
Use the new 6-pin cable that ships with AMS HT.

data.name: Bambu Lab AMS lite
data.compatibility_notes: A series only. One AMS lite per printer, and it cannot be mixed with AMS, AMS 2 Pro or AMS HT. Not compatible with X1 or P1. The A2L can run 1 AMS lite plus up to 4 AMS units.

drying.note: No heater and no desiccant system. Recommended ambient is 10 to 30 C and under 85 percent humidity.

notes: TPU rated 77D, 55D or harder can feed. TPU at 95A, 85A, 83A, 80A or softer cannot.
Absorbent PVA is not advised. Third party CF and GF filament breaks or damages the feeder channel. Only tougher grades such as Bambu PLA-CF and PETG-CF are compatible.

The material table lists ABS and ABS-GF as not recommended on AMS lite, and PLA Glow as not recommended. It lists ASA and PC as compatible with AMS and AMS lite, but the A1 series is an open frame printer where Bambu rates them not recommended.
The material table marks PVA and BVOH compatible while the AMS lite FAQ says avoid absorbent PVA. See disagreements.
PET-CF and PET-GF are not compatible. Use the external spool for nylon and fiber grades.

rfid.detail: One RFID coil per slot. Reading on insertion is on by default and cannot be turned off.

features: Single stage feeder into the toolhead. No filament buffer is needed.
Tangle detection module above the toolhead pauses on high feed resistance.
Each rotary holder turns up to 150 degrees to tighten the spool on unload, so long filament cannot be rewound.
Filament backup switches to a slot with the same brand, type and color when one runs out.

known_issues.symptom: False tangle alarms or feeding failures
known_issues.cause: PTFE tubes too long or too bent. The feeder pushes up to 1.2 m.

fix.advice: Place the AMS lite about 50 mm from the printer. The A1 mini combo tubes are 580 mm and 700 mm; A1 tubes are 730 mm and 850 mm. Cut long tubes shorter.

known_issues.symptom: AMS lite wobbles or tips during prints
known_issues.cause: Heavy spools in the upper slots.

fix.advice: Put heavier spools in slots 2 and 3. It cannot be wall mounted.

known_issues.symptom: Flexible or brittle filament will not load
known_issues.cause: The single stage feeder cannot handle soft or brittle material.

fix.advice: Print those from the external spool holder.

positions.claim: Compatible, because Bambu PLA-CF and PETG-CF are tougher grades
Not recommended on AMS lite, compatible on AMS

disagreements.resolution: List as not recommended. This is the more conservative reading.

disagreements.topic: PVA and BVOH on AMS lite

positions.claim: Avoid absorbent PVA in AMS lite

disagreements.resolution: List as not recommended. Use the external spool for PVA.

hotend.swap_system: Induction hotend rack that changes hotends automatically

power.mains: 100 to 120 V AC and 200 to 240 V AC, 50/60 Hz

max_w.note: At 220 V. 1250 W at 110 V. The bed holds maximum heater power for no more than 3 minutes.

printing_typical_w.note: Bambu wiki average power for a test print. The kWh figures equal the average watts, so the test appears to run about one hour. Duration is not stated.

Bambu wiki PETG test print
Bambu wiki PC test print

multi_material.note: Needs the H2 series dedicated 4-in-1 PTFE adapter for multiple units.

pilot_notes: Dual nozzle printer with an induction hotend rack. Nozzle offset calibration runs for the toolhead hotend and every rack hotend, so it takes longer with more hotends.
Spec lists a single flow figure (40 mm3/s). No high flow hotend is stated on the spec sheet.

data.name: Bambu Lab H2D
data.status_note: Listed in the Bambu US store in 2026-09, also sold as an AMS combo and a Laser Full Combo.

build_volume_mm.note: Each nozzle reaches a different area. A print that uses both nozzles must fit in the 300 mm wide overlap.

hotend.high_flow_note: Standard flow hotend 40 mm3/s, optional high flow hotend 65 mm3/s (Bambu test on ABS at 280 C). A TPU high flow hotend also has an Orca variant.
hotend.note: Replace nozzles on the printer, then sync the nozzle info. Bambu Studio treats the nozzle field as display only.

bed.note: Spec lists Textured PEI and Smooth PEI. Bambu also lists the 350 x 320 mm size for H2D and H2S. The bed holds maximum heater power for no more than 3 minutes.

enclosure.note: Orca supports chamber temperature control on H2D. It does not flag air filtration support in the machine profile even though Bambu lists the HEPA and carbon path.

power.mains: 100 to 120 V AC and 200 to 240 V AC, 50/60 Hz

max_w.note: At 220 V. 1320 W at 110 V. The bed holds maximum heater power for no more than 3 minutes.

printing_typical_w.note: Bambu wiki average power for a test print. The kWh figures equal the average watts, so the test appears to run about one hour. Duration is not stated.

idle_w.note: Bambu wiki reading without network connection. 25 to 27 W with Wi-Fi.

measured_examples.job: Bambu wiki PLA test print
Bambu wiki PETG test print
Bambu wiki PC test print

power.note: Chamber heating is active but no chamber heater wattage is published. After Low Power Mode starts, Bambu says H series peak power is about 860 W.

values: 2200 W at 220 V and 1320 W at 110 V (H2D spec sheet)
1800 W and 1250 W (Bambu wiki 'H2 Series' column)
disagreements.resolution: Use the H2D spec sheet. The wiki H2 column matches the H2C spec sheet, not the H2D.

values: 1050 W at 220 V and 110 V (H2D spec sheet 'Average Power', undefined)
disagreements.resolution: Use the wiki figure for printing. The spec sheet does not say what the average covers.

data.sensors_note: Nozzle camera reads nozzle clumping, air printing and spaghetti. The Laser Edition adds a BirdsEye camera and flame detection. The toolhead force (eddy current) sensor feeds flow dynamics.

builtin_calibrations.what: Auto K value. Purges at the wiper and reads extrusion force with the toolhead eddy current sensor. Bambu sets the auto K higher than a manual pattern value to avoid corner bulging.
Nozzle offset calibration measures the offset between the two nozzles with a sensor and compensates bed height. The ideal height difference is 5 mm.
Bed leveling and print calibration from Settings, Calibration.

multi_material.note: Filament buffer is built in. A 4-in-1 PTFE adapter is needed for 3 or more units, or 2 units plus an external spool. One unit can dry from printer power; more need power adapters.
Needs external power to dry. Up to 25 colors in the extreme case (4 x 4 + 8 x 1 + external spool).
The FAQ says AMS and AMS 2 Pro can print together on X1, P1, H2D and H2S.

materials.note: Spec: PLA, PETG, TPU, PVA, BVOH, ABS, ASA, PC, PA, PET and fiber reinforced PLA, PETG, PA, PET, PC, ABS, ASA, PPA-CF/GF, PPS. TPU 85A is not recommended on high flow nozzles per the material table.

profile_baseline.note: Values shown are for the standard flow nozzle. The high flow variants raise outer wall speed to 500, inner wall to 600 and infill to 600.

pilot_notes: Two nozzles. Every filament is assigned to the left or right nozzle. The bed moves about 5 mm when the active nozzle changes, so keep filaments on one nozzle where the plan allows.
A print that uses both nozzles has a 300 mm wide area. Single nozzle prints can use 325 mm.
Active chamber heating to 65 C. For ABS, ASA, PC, PA and CF grades mimir may set chamber_temperature and activate_chamber_temp_control. Turn it off for PLA, PETG and TPU.
For PLA and PETG with the chamber warming, Bambu says remove the top glass lid (PLA above 45 C bed, PETG above 70 C).
Time-lapse on H2 series: the printer picks a main nozzle per layer and moves to the purge chute for shots from the other nozzle.
Nozzle camera AI can stop a print for spaghetti, clumping or air printing. Expect pause events.
Print history and cover images for the LAN tools need Store Sent Files on External Storage plus a USB drive.
Nozzle swaps are physical. After any nozzle change, sync nozzle info on the printer and rerun flow dynamics.

common_issues.symptom: Wrong or missing colors after a nozzle switch on dual nozzle prints
common_issues.cause: Nozzle offset out of calibration.

fix.advice: Run Nozzle Offset Calibration from the printer (Settings, Calibration).

common_issues.symptom: Filament clogs in the hotend with a warm chamber
common_issues.cause: PLA or TPU running with active chamber heating on.

fix.why: Low temperature filaments do not need a heated chamber.

fix.advice: Take the top glass off for PLA above 45 C bed.

common_issues.symptom: Auto flow dynamics K value differs from a manual pattern
common_issues.cause: Bambu sets the auto K higher on H2D to prevent corner stacking.

fix.advice: Trust the auto value first. Compare corner quality before overriding it with a lower manual value.

data.name: Bambu Lab H2S

power.mains: 100 to 120 V AC and 200 to 240 V AC, 50/60 Hz

max_w.note: At 220 V. 1170 W at 110 V. The bed holds maximum heater power for no more than 3 minutes.

printing_typical_w.note: Bambu wiki average power for a test print. The kWh figures equal the average watts, so the test appears to run about one hour. Duration is not stated.

idle_w.note: Bambu wiki reading without network connection. 26.5 W with Wi-Fi.

measured_examples.job: Bambu wiki PLA test print
Bambu wiki PETG test print
Bambu wiki PC test print

power.note: Bambu says H series peak power is about 860 W once Low Power Mode starts.

multi_material.note: Single nozzle. Up to 24 colors. Two AMS units need a 4-in-1 PTFE adapter.

pilot_notes: Single nozzle H2 series printer. Same chamber heater, filtration and speed class as the H2D but one toolhead.
Chamber temperature control is supported. Use chamber_temperature only for ABS, ASA, PC, PA and CF grades.

data.name: Bambu Lab P1P
data.status_note: Not in the Bambu US store new printer list in 2026-09.

max_flow_mm3s.note: Bambu test: 150 x 150 mm single wall, Bambu ABS at 280 C.

enclosure.note: Open frame with printable modplate panels. Auxiliary part cooling fan, control board fan, chamber regulator fan and air filter are optional. Orca marks no auxiliary fan.

printing_typical_w.note: Bambu wiki average power over a short test print (about 16 minutes).

idle_w.note: Bambu wiki reading without network connection. 5 to 5.6 W with Wi-Fi.

Bambu wiki test print, ABS, 16 min 3 s

builtin_calibrations.what: Manual K pattern only.
Auto bed leveling and auto Z offset adjustment.
Vibration suppression calibration.

multi_material.needs: filament buffer for one unit or AMS Hub for more

materials.note: Spec: PLA, PETG, TPU, PVA, PET ideal; PA, PC, ABS, ASA capable; carbon or glass fiber not recommended. Bambu's table marks ABS, ASA, PC and PA as not recommended on open frame printers.

pilot_notes: Open frame. Warn before ABS, ASA, PC and nylon: they curl and split without an enclosure. Offer PETG or an enclosure kit first.
No auxiliary part cooling fan by default. Overhangs and bridges in PLA cool worse than on the P1S. Suggest slower overhangs or the auxiliary fan kit.
No lidar and no auto flow dynamics. Use the manual K pattern.
The heatbed tops out at 100 C.
Stock nozzle is stainless steel. Block fiber filled filament until a hardened hotend is fitted.

common_issues.symptom: ABS or ASA parts warp and split
common_issues.cause: Open frame loses heat and drafts hit the print.

fix.advice: Print ABS or ASA only with an enclosure kit, or switch to PETG.

fix.why: A brim holds corners down on a cold chamber.

common_issues.symptom: Poor bridges and overhangs on PLA
common_issues.cause: No auxiliary part cooling fan.

fix.why: Use all the cooling the printer has on overhangs.
Slower bridges give the single fan time to set the plastic.

data.name: Bambu Lab P1S
data.status_note: Listed in the Bambu US store in 2026-09.

build_volume_mm.note: Studio defaults to 250 mm to protect the heatbed. The collapsible filament cutter stopper can occupy part of the plate when popped out.

max_flow_mm3s.note: Bambu test: 150 x 150 mm single wall, Bambu ABS at 280 C.

hotend.note: Spec says stainless steel nozzle stock and not recommended for carbon or glass fiber. A hardened steel hotend is a separate purchase (shared X1 and P1 hotend page).

enclosure.note: Plastic and glass shell. Auxiliary part fan and carbon filter included. Top lid comes off for PLA, PETG and TPU.

motion.note: Bambu calls it vibration suppression and lists it in the calibration menu with motor noise cancellation and auto bed leveling.

printing_typical_w.note: Bambu wiki average power over a short test print (about 16 minutes). Power factor 0.45 to 0.64.

idle_w.note: Bambu wiki reading without network connection. 5.8 to 6 W with Wi-Fi.

Bambu wiki test print, ABS, 16 min 3 s

data.sensors_note: Camera is low rate (1280 x 720, 0.5 fps). No lidar, no nozzle camera, no door sensor listed, no spaghetti detection listed on the spec sheet.

builtin_calibrations.what: Manual K pattern only. Auto flow dynamics is not available on P1.
Auto bed leveling and auto Z offset adjustment.
Vibration suppression calibration.
Motor noise cancellation.

multi_material.needs: filament buffer for one unit or AMS Hub for more
own power adapter per unit for drying

materials.note: Spec: PLA, PETG, TPU, ABS, ASA, PVA, PET ideal; PA and PC capable; fiber reinforced not recommended with the stock stainless nozzle. Fiber grades need a hardened hotend and are possible with that swap only.

pilot_notes: For PLA, PLA-CF, PVA and TPU with the bed above 45 C, tell the user to remove the top glass lid. For PETG and PETG-CF the threshold is 70 C. ABS and ASA stay closed.
No lidar. Flow dynamics must be run in manual mode (K pattern). Do not plan an auto calibration.
Stock nozzle is stainless steel. Block carbon fiber and glass fiber jobs until the user confirms a hardened nozzle.
The chamber is passive. ABS and ASA are rated ideal by Bambu with the door shut. PA and PC are listed as capable, not ideal.
Default max height in Studio is 250 mm, not 256 mm.
Bambu documents the Micro SD card requirement for LAN only printing on X series printers. The P1 section of the same page does not mention it.

common_issues.symptom: PLA jams or the extruder clicks on long prints with the lid on
common_issues.cause: Heat creep. The passive chamber warms above PLA's softening point once the bed is hot.

fix.advice: Remove the top glass lid and open the door for PLA when the bed is above 45 C, as Bambu recommends. Use a lower bed temperature on a smooth or textured PEI plate.

common_issues.symptom: K value from pattern looks wrong or bounces between filaments
common_issues.cause: P1 uses manual flow dynamics only.

fix.advice: Run the manual K pattern for each spool type and store the value in the filament profile or the AMS slot.

data.name: Bambu Lab P2S

bed.note: Reads second generation plate QR codes. First generation plates work but are not recognized.

motion.note: The Orca machine profile carries 1000 mm/s. Spec sheet says 600.

power.mains: 100 to 120 V AC and 200 to 240 V AC, 50/60 Hz

max_w.note: At 220 V. 1000 W at 110 V. The bed holds maximum heater power for a short time to reach temperature.

printing_typical_w.note: Bambu lists 200 W steady state for PLA printing at both 220 V and 110 V.

standby_w.note: Offline standby. 7.8 to 8.2 W with Wi-Fi.

multi_material.needs: P2S filament buffer (included in the P2S Combo). A 4-in-1 adapter for 3 or more units.

pilot_notes: Enclosed with a passive chamber and a hardened steel nozzle stock. Fiber filled filament is fine on the stock nozzle.
When the printer powers an AMS 2 Pro for drying without a power adapter, it cannot heat the bed or hotend or move axes during drying.
Bambu Studio Print sends the file to internal storage; LAN tools may not read cover images unless the print is sent to a card.

data.name: Bambu Lab X1 Carbon
data.status_note: Not in the Bambu US store new printer list in 2026-09. Only a refurbished X1C listing remains. Firmware and wiki support continue.

build_volume_mm.note: Spec is 256 mm. Bambu Studio and the Orca profile default to 250 mm height to protect the heatbed.

hotend.high_flow_note: The Orca machine profile lists a High Flow variant, but the Bambu hotend page offers only hardened steel and stainless steel hotends. Not confirmed.

max_flow_mm3s.note: Bambu test: 150 x 150 mm single wall, Bambu ABS at 280 C.

bed.note: 110 C on 220 V mains, 120 C on 110 V. Textured PEI and SuperTack work but second generation QR codes are not recognized on X1 (choose Resolved on screen or turn off build plate detection).

enclosure.note: No chamber heater. The heatbed warms the chamber. The top glass lid comes off for low temperature filaments (see bambu_plates).

motion.note: Bambu calls it vibration compensation. It runs as part of the startup calibration.

printing_typical_w.note: Bambu wiki average power over a short test print (about 15 to 17 minutes). Power factor 0.45 to 0.63.

idle_w.note: Bambu wiki reading without network connection. 8.7 to 9.9 W with Wi-Fi. Screen state not stated.

measured_examples.job: Bambu wiki test print, PLA, 15 min 24 s
Bambu wiki test print, ABS, 17 min 24 s

builtin_calibrations.what: Auto pressure advance (K value) by printing lines and scanning them with Micro Lidar. Stored per filament in the printer.
Auto flow ratio calibration with Micro Lidar. X series only.
Automatic bed leveling and first layer Z offset check.
Maps resonance to cancel ghosting and ringing. Rerun after moving the printer.
Motor noise cancellation calibration.

multi_material.needs: filament buffer for one unit or AMS Hub for two or more
same buffer or hub, each unit needs its own power adapter to dry
same buffer or hub, external power for drying

materials.note: Spec sheet: PLA, PETG, TPU, ABS, ASA, PET supported; PA and PC ideal; carbon and glass fiber ideal (hardened nozzle stock). TPU 85A is very soft: feed from the external spool, slowly. HIPS and PP are not covered by Bambu's tables.

pilot_notes: PLA, PLA-CF, PVA and TPU: if the bed is above 45 C, tell the user to take off the top glass lid. For PETG and PETG-CF the threshold is 70 C. Keep the lid and door closed for ABS, ASA, PC and PA.
The chamber has no heater. For ABS, ASA, PC and PA the bed is the only heat source, so keep the door shut and skip the top lid removal.
Flow dynamics and flow rate auto calibration use the lidar. They fail on transparent, sparkle, marble, metal and silk filament, and on TPU. Use the manual K pattern or manual flow test for those.
Starting a print from Bambu Studio in LAN only mode needs a Micro SD card in the printer.
Bambu Studio treats the nozzle field as display only in recent versions. If the user swaps to a different diameter or material, the change is physical, then sync on the printer.

Third party plates (SuperTack, textured PEI) are not auto recognized by X1 firmware. If the plate warning appears, choose Resolved on screen. Bambu suggests turning off build plate position detection for SuperTack.
Purged filament falls down the rear waste chute. Multi color plans need a container and an empty chute.
After moving the printer, after maintenance or after a firmware update, suggest the printer calibration (bed leveling, vibration compensation).

common_issues.symptom: Auto flow dynamics gives odd or inconsistent K values
common_issues.cause: Damp filament, transparent or metallic finish, dirty or slick plate so the lines do not stick, worn nozzle, or TPU. Results also vary by about 10 percent run to run.

fix.advice: Dry the spool, wash the plate (or add glue stick) and rerun. For transparent or sparkle filament use the manual K pattern.
Ignore differences under about 10 percent between runs. Bambu measured that much jitter.

common_issues.symptom: Plate warning or first layer trouble after fitting a SuperTack or textured PEI plate
common_issues.cause: X1 firmware does not read second generation plate QR codes.

fix.advice: Choose Resolved on the printer screen, or turn off build plate position detection under Controls, Print Options.

common_issues.symptom: Purge waste jams the chute on long multi color prints
common_issues.cause: Purged filament piles up under the chute or a cover blocks it.

fix.advice: Put a large container under the chute, keep it uncovered, and empty it during long prints.

fix.why: Bambu says default flush volumes run slightly high. Test that colors stay clean before going lower.

Auto flow ratio with Micro Lidar.
Automatic bed leveling.
Resonance mapping.

multi_material.needs: filament buffer for one unit or AMS Hub for more
own power adapter per unit for drying

materials.note: Spec: PA, PC, ABS, ASA, PET and fiber reinforced grades are superior; PPA-CF/GF and PPS grades are ideal. Bambu's material table lists PPS as X1E and H2 only.

pilot_notes: This is the X1 family printer with a real chamber heater. For ABS, ASA, PC, PA and CF grades mimir may set chamber_temperature (up to 60 C) and turn on activate_chamber_temp_control.
Use the HEPA and carbon filter path for ABS, ASA and PA by turning on activate_air_filtration in the filament profile.
Same lidar limits as the X1C: auto flow calibration is unreliable on transparent, sparkle and silk filament and on TPU.
Ethernet is available. A LAN only, Developer Mode setup is common for X1E because it targets isolated networks.
Starting a print from Bambu Studio in LAN only mode needs a Micro SD card, as on other X series printers.

common_issues.symptom: PLA or PETG clogs or strings with the chamber heater on
common_issues.cause: Chamber heat softens filament above the heatbreak. Orca lists PLA as softening near 45 C.

fix.why: Low temperature filaments do not need a heated chamber.

fix.advice: Open the door and remove the top glass lid for PLA, PLA-CF and TPU. For PETG do so when the bed is above 70 C.

data.name: Bambu Lab X2D

extruder.auxiliary: stepper motor extruder, listed as Bowden in the Orca profile

power.mains: High voltage version 200 to 240 V AC, low voltage version 100 to 120 V AC, 50/60 Hz

max_w.note: At 220 V. 1100 W on the 110 V version.

printing_typical_w.note: Bambu steady state power at 25 C ambient, same at 220 V and 110 V.

standby_w.note: Offline standby. 7.8 to 8.2 W with Wi-Fi.

power.note: Bambu lists a Low Power Mode with approximately 750 W peak. No chamber heater wattage is published.

multi_material.needs: Filament buffer included. 4-in-1 PTFE adapter II for more than 2 units.

pilot_notes: Bambu says to print PLA Silk, PETG-CF, ASA-CF, PA6-CF and TPU for AMS with the main hotend when quality matters. The auxiliary hotend is for the other filaments in the spec list.
The Bambu material table marks ABS on the auxiliary hotend as not recommended.

data.name: Creality K1 Max

extruder.note: Dual gear direct drive on all K1 series.

hotend.stock_nozzle: 0.4 mm hardened steel tip copper alloy (K1C and later K1 Max units); early K1 units shipped a brass nozzle
hotend.note: K1C states a hardened steel tip stock. Early K1 and K1 Max shipped brass; Creality sold a hardened nozzle kit. Check the user's unit.

bed.note: Flexible PEI sheet on the 300 x 300 bed.

enclosure.note: Fully enclosed on the K1C; the K1 and K1 Max are open at the top under a clear lid. Open the lid for PLA on any K1.

motion.note: Orca limits 800 mm/s and 20000 mm/s2. Creality states 600 mm/s and 20000 mm/s2 for typical prints. Built in accelerometer runs an auto shaper calibration.

power.mains: 100 to 120 V AC and 200 to 240 V AC, 50/60 Hz

max_w.note: Maximum draw per a retailer FAQ.

psu_rated_w.note: 24 V 6.25 A supply for mainboard, motors, fans and hotend. The bed runs from mains.

builtin_calibrations.what: Automatic bed leveling before each print.
Built in accelerometer based shaper calibration from the touchscreen.
Creality Print offers flow and PA calibration tests.

multi_material.note: Orca has K1 Max_CFS-C profiles. Confirm the printer accepts the CFS firmware.

materials.note: 100 C bed and passive chamber suit ABS and ASA only on the K1C or with the lid closed. Do not assume a hardened nozzle.

profile_baseline.note: Only the CFS-C K1 Max 0.20 Standard profile is bundled in Orca at this commit; K1C has an equivalent (outer wall 200, inner wall 250, accel 10000 with outer wall 3000).

pilot_notes: K1, K1 Max and K1C use vendor Klipper on an embedded board. Root can be enabled in settings; community helper scripts add Moonraker, Fluidd and macros. Do not assume Moonraker is present on an unrooted printer.
K1C differs from K1 Max: 220 x 220 x 250 volume, enclosed chamber, hardened tip nozzle, tougher part cooling. K1 (non Max) matches K1C size with an open top.
Print speed claims (600 to 800 mm/s) are peaks. Real speed is flow limited to roughly what the hotend melts, so keep the max volumetric speed of the filament profile.
Klipper flavor. Pressure advance via SET_PRESSURE_ADVANCE; Creality macros define PRINT_START. Check the argument names before editing machine_start_gcode.
Open the lid for PLA and TPU; a closed K1 chamber heats above 40 C quickly and softens PLA.

common_issues.symptom: Ringing on walls at default profile
common_issues.cause: High acceleration and a lightweight gantry.

fix.why: The K1C profile uses 3000 for outer walls.

fix.advice: Rerun the built in input shaper calibration.

common_issues.symptom: Nozzle clog with PLA in a closed chamber
common_issues.cause: Heat creep in a hot chamber.

fix.advice: Open the lid and remove the top cover for PLA.

common_issues.symptom: Stringing with PETG
common_issues.cause: Hot nozzle and long travel at high speed.

fix.why: Cooler PETG strings less.
A little more retraction on direct drive.

data.name: Creality K2 Plus

bed.note: Bed maximum is from memory of the Creality spec, not re-verified in this pass.

enclosure.note: Actively heated chamber to 60 C, and an air purifier. The chamber temperature is set in Creality software; Orca profiles mark chamber temperature control as supported.

motion.note: Orca limits 800 mm/s and 30000 mm/s2. Creality quotes a typical 300 mm/s; peak claims run to 600. Built in G-sensor for shaper calibration.

hotend_heater_w.note: Creality states the high flow hotend is powered by a 100 W heater.

builtin_calibrations.what: Automatic bed leveling and nozzle calibration.
Built in G-sensor calibration.

multi_material.note: CFS holds 4 spools per unit. The K2 Plus supports up to 4 CFS units for 16 colors; Creality states this on the K2 series page, confirm before promising it.

materials.note: 60 C chamber and a 350 C hotend cover ABS, ASA, PC and PA. PLA and TPU need the chamber off and the lid cracked. CFS itself is limited to normal filaments; use the external spool holder for engineering materials.

profile_baseline.note: Orca's default process for this printer is 0.16mm Optimal; the 0.20mm Standard is the closest match to a generic 0.20 profile.

pilot_notes: Chamber temperature is active. chamber_temperature is valid, capped at 60 C. Do not set it for PLA, PETG or TPU.
Klipper based Creality OS with Moonraker and Fluidd present. SSH is enabled from the Root account information setting; this is Creality's own switch. Community tooling exists but is not required.
Creality Print is the vendor slicer and drives CFS material mapping and the K2 G-code most directly. Orca profiles exist and work; flag that CFS color mapping is more complete in Creality Print.
Creality's Klipper modifications are the subject of open source compliance discussion, so behavior can differ from upstream Klipper. Verify a command exists before relying on it.
Klipper flavor. Confirm PRINT_START argument names before editing machine_start_gcode.

common_issues.symptom: PLA jams or blobs after the chamber heated
common_issues.cause: Chamber heat soaks the extruder.

fix.why: Keep the chamber cool for PLA.

fix.advice: Open the lid and door for PLA and TPU.

common_issues.symptom: Warped ABS or ASA corners
common_issues.cause: Chamber not warm enough at print start.

fix.why: A warm chamber reduces warping for ABS and ASA.
Less cooling keeps layers fused.

common_issues.symptom: Filament tangle or CFS jam
common_issues.cause: Spool tangled or unsupported filament in the CFS.

fix.advice: Use the external spool holder for TPU, engineering and abrasive filaments.

data.name: Elegoo Centauri Carbon

hotend.note: Search summaries of the Elegoo page and reviews say 320 C. Some listings say 300 C; use 300 for safety in profiles unless the user has confirmed 320.

enclosure.note: Fully enclosed steel, aluminum and glass shell. No heated chamber.

motion.note: Orca limits 500 mm/s and 20000 mm/s2. Elegoo firmware runs its own calibration at start.

bed_heater_w.note: AC heated bed, 1000 W at 220 V. The 110 V figure is not stated.

builtin_calibrations.what: Automatic bed leveling and nozzle calibration before print.
Vendor firmware vibration compensation; procedure and accelerometer details not verified.

multi_material.note: Elegoo's CANVAS multicolor add on. Orca support is limited; details not verified.

materials.note: Hardened nozzle and enclosure allow ABS, ASA and CF filaments. No chamber heater and a 110 C bed limit PC and warp prone nylon. Open the lid for PLA.

profile_baseline.note: Orca's Elegoo profile sets inner wall and travel acceleration to 0, which means fall back to the default of 10000.

pilot_notes: Firmware status is contested and I could only confirm it through reporting and community docs, not a manufacturer statement. Reported: stock Elegoo OS is a heavily modified Klipper; Elegoo released source only after community pressure and the release raised license questions (All3DP). Moonraker, Fluidd and macro access are not offered by stock firmware.

Community firmware exists: OpenCentauri COSMOS (full Klipper and Kalico replacement on the stock mainboard) and a patched Elegoo firmware. These are unofficial, flashing carries brick and warranty risk, and mimir must not walk a user through flashing without saying so.
On stock firmware do not offer Klipper macro or Moonraker automation. Print start behavior is fixed; send G-code from Orca using Elegoo's LAN protocol or file transfer.
Slicer G-code flavor is klipper in Orca but stock start G-code is vendor controlled. Keep machine_start_gcode unchanged unless the user runs COSMOS.
No chamber heater: do not set chamber_temperature.

common_issues.symptom: Ringing or ghosting on fast prints
common_issues.cause: Default accelerations are high for the lightweight gantry.

fix.why: Lower outer wall acceleration to clean up ringing.

common_issues.symptom: PLA jams after long ABS runs
common_issues.cause: Enclosed chamber heat soak.

fix.advice: Open the lid and let the chamber cool for PLA.

common_issues.symptom: Cannot reach Moonraker or Fluidd
common_issues.cause: Stock firmware does not expose them.

fix.advice: Use Elegoo's own app or LAN upload. Moonraker access needs community firmware such as OpenCentauri COSMOS, at the user's own risk.

data.name: Elegoo Neptune 4 Pro

build_volume_mm.note: Orca profile uses a 230 x 230 printable area; Elegoo lists 225.

hotend.note: Elegoo lists 300 C. Hardened steel is not stock; add one before abrasive filaments.

bed.note: Segmented heatbed with a flexible PEI sheet. Bed maximum is from a search summary of the Elegoo page.

enclosure.note: Open frame bedslinger.

motion.note: Orca limits 500 mm/s and 10000 mm/s2. Elegoo advertises 500 mm/s. Klipper input shaper is configured with default values; recalibration needs an accelerometer.

psu_rated_w.note: A community owner calls it a 400 W supply. Elegoo does not publish the rating on its store page.

bed_heater_w.note: Two zones, 100 W and 150 W. The outer zone turns on only when the model needs it.

heatup_peak_w.note: Owner reading with hotend at 200 C and both bed zones at 60 C. Above 80 percent of the supply rating.

printing_typical_w.note: Owner reading of the 18 minute supplied Benchy, mostly 78 to 85 W. Bed heaters pushed it to about 230 W for part of the print. One unit, one wattmeter.

idle_w.note: Booted, steppers not holding. 22.5 W once the steppers hold after homing.

builtin_calibrations.what: 121 point automatic bed mesh.
Factory input shaper present; retune needs an accelerometer.

materials.note: Open frame: ABS and ASA need an enclosure and a draft free room; nylon and PC are out of practical range. CF and GF need a hardened nozzle.

pilot_notes: Bedslinger: high acceleration with a heavy bed moves the part. Tall parts with a small base wobble at high acceleration.
Klipper flavor, Moonraker and Fluidd available. Pressure advance via SET_PRESSURE_ADVANCE. Confirm PRINT_START argument names.
Open frame with no enclosure, so no ABS or ASA advice without the user adding one.
Hotend flow and part cooling cap real speed well below 500 mm/s. Keep filament_max_volumetric_speed at or below the profile.

common_issues.symptom: Ringing or ghosting on walls
common_issues.cause: Bedslinger mass and default acceleration.

fix.why: Bedslingers ring sooner; lower outer wall acceleration.
Slower outer walls print cleaner on a bedslinger.

common_issues.symptom: First layer uneven on parts of the bed
common_issues.cause: Warped bed or mesh drift.

fix.advice: Rerun the bed mesh with the bed hot and check the Z offset.

common_issues.symptom: Filament grinds or under extrudes at speed
common_issues.cause: Hotend cannot melt fast enough.

fix.advice: Run a max flow test and cap filament_max_volumetric_speed below the failure point.

data.name: Prusa CORE One

hotend.note: Orca has CORE One HF profiles for the high flow nozzle. CORE One L is a larger sibling with its own profiles and is not covered by this file.

bed.note: Magnetic steel sheet. Bed maximum is from Prusa's family spec, not re-verified for the CORE One page.

enclosure.note: Actively regulated chamber to 55 C using bed heat and an internal fan and vents. Prusa sells a separate filter; not confirmed here, so treat filtration as unknown.

motion.note: Orca machine limits 350 mm/s and 7000 mm/s2. Input shaper is on; recalibration and phase stepping calibration need the accelerometer set on the base CORE One.

printing_typical_w.note: Prusa stated power consumption for PLA and ABS settings. Measurement method not given.

builtin_calibrations.what: Live Z adjust from the LCD.
Accelerometer set required on the base CORE One.
LCD Menu, Settings, Phase Stepping, Calibration; needs the accelerometer set on the base CORE One.

multi_material.note: Enclosed MMU3 kit for CORE One.

materials.note: Enclosed with active chamber, so ABS and ASA are first class. PLA in a hot chamber can soften in the extruder path: open the lid or lower chamber_temperature for PLA. Abrasive filaments need a hardened nozzle.

pilot_notes: Chamber temperature is active. chamber_temperature and activate_chamber_temp_control are valid here, capped at 55 C. Let the chamber reach temperature before starting ABS or ASA.
Do not raise chamber temperature for PLA, PETG or TPU. Warm chambers cause heat creep and soft filament.
G-code flavor is marlin2, pressure advance via M572.
